claim: All fossils came from Upper Devonian Wutong Formation at Jianchuan mine in Xinhang town, Guangde City, Anhui Province, China.
source: All fossils came from Upper Devonian Wutong Formation at Jianchuan mine in Xinhang town, Guangde City, Anhui Province, China.
evidence: Direct statement about the geological source and location of the fossils studied.

claim: At Jianchuan mine, Wutong Formation consists of Guanshan Member with quartzose sandstone and a little mudstone, and the overlying Leigutai Member with inter-beds of quartzose sandstone, siltstone and mudstone.
source: At Jianchuan mine, Wutong Formation consists of Guanshan Member with quartzose sandstone and a little mudstone, and the overlying Leigutai Member with inter-beds of quartzose sandstone, siltstone and mudstone.
evidence: Direct description of the stratigraphic composition at the study site.

claim: Spore analysis indicates that the Leigutai Member here is late Famennian in age.
source: Spore analysis indicates that the Leigutai Member here is late Famennian in age (Gao et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by cited spore analysis study.

claim: Progymnosperm Archaeopteris and lycopsid Leptophloeum occur in Leigutai and/or Guanshan members.
source: Progymnosperm Archaeopteris and lycopsid Leptophloeum occur in Leigutai and/or Guanshan members, and they were distributed worldwide in the Late Devonian (Taylor et al., 2009).
evidence: Direct observation of fossil occurrence with citation supporting their Late Devonian distribution.

claim: Archaeopteris and Leptophloeum were distributed worldwide in the Late Devonian.
source: Progymnosperm Archaeopteris and lycopsid Leptophloeum occur in Leigutai and/or Guanshan members, and they were distributed worldwide in the Late Devonian (Taylor et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Taylor et al., 2009.

claim: Fernlike plant Xinhangia was found at the basal part of Leigutai Member.
source: Fernlike plant Xinhangia (Yang and Wang, 2022) and lycopsid Sublepidodendron (Xu et al., 2022) were found at the basal part of Leigutai Member.
evidence: Direct statement of fossil occurrence with citation.

claim: Lycopsid Sublepidodendron was found at the basal part of Leigutai Member.
source: Fernlike plant Xinhangia (Yang and Wang, 2022) and lycopsid Sublepidodendron (Xu et al., 2022) were found at the basal part of Leigutai Member.
evidence: Direct statement of fossil occurrence with citation.

claim: In situ lycopsid trees of Guangdedendron with stigmarian rooting system appear in multiple horizons of Leigutai Member.
source: In situ lycopsid trees of Guangdedendron with stigmarian rooting system appear in multiple horizons of Leigutai Member and they formed the Xinhang forest (Wang et al., 2019; Gao et al., 2022).
evidence: Direct observation of fossil occurrence with citations.

claim: Guangdedendron trees formed the Xinhang forest.
source: In situ lycopsid trees of Guangdedendron with stigmarian rooting system appear in multiple horizons of Leigutai Member and they formed the Xinhang forest (Wang et al., 2019; Gao et al., 2022).
evidence: Direct statement with supporting citations.

claim: Numerous ovules of Alasemenia were collected from many horizons of siltstone and mudstone of Wutong Formation (Leigutai Member) at Jianchuan mine.
source: From many horizons of siltstone and mudstone of Wutong Formation (Leigutai Member) at Jianchuan mine, numerous ovules of Alasemenia were collected (Figure 1, Figure 2, Figure 3) and some were transversely sectioned to show the ovular structure (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Figure 4—figure supplement 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Direct statement of fossil collection with references to figures showing the specimens.

claim: Some Alasemenia ovules were transversely sectioned to show the ovular structure.
source: From many horizons of siltstone and mudstone of Wutong Formation (Leigutai Member) at Jianchuan mine, numerous ovules of Alasemenia were collected (Figure 1, Figure 2, Figure 3) and some were transversely sectioned to show the ovular structure (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Figure 4—figure supplement 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Direct statement with references to figures showing sectioned specimens.

claim: The generic name Alasemenia is from the Latin 'ala' and 'semen', meaning wing and seed, respectively.
source: The generic name from the Latin 'ala' and 'semen', meaning wing and seed, respectively; the specific epithet from the Latin 'tri' (three), referring to wing number of a seed.
evidence: Direct statement of etymology.

claim: The specific epithet 'tria' is from the Latin 'tri' (three), referring to wing number of a seed.
source: The generic name from the Latin 'ala' and 'semen', meaning wing and seed, respectively; the specific epithet from the Latin 'tri' (three), referring to wing number of a seed.
evidence: Direct statement of etymology.

claim: The holotype of Alasemenia tria is PKUB21721a, b (part and counterpart).
source: PKUB21721a, b (part and counterpart housed in Department of Geology, Peking University, Beijing) (Figure 1a, m and n).
evidence: Direct designation of holotype specimen.

claim: The holotype is housed in Department of Geology, Peking University, Beijing.
source: PKUB21721a, b (part and counterpart housed in Department of Geology, Peking University, Beijing) (Figure 1a, m and n).
evidence: Direct statement of specimen repository.

claim: The locality of Alasemenia tria is Xinhang, Guangde, Anhui, China.
source: Xinhang, Guangde, Anhui, China; Leigutai Member of Wutong Formation, Upper Devonian.
evidence: Direct statement of fossil locality.

claim: The horizon of Alasemenia tria is Leigutai Member of Wutong Formation, Upper Devonian.
source: Xinhang, Guangde, Anhui, China; Leigutai Member of Wutong Formation, Upper Devonian.
evidence: Direct statement of stratigraphic horizon.

claim: Alasemenia has dichotomous branches bearing terminal and acupulate ovules.
source: Dichotomous branches bearing terminal and acupulate ovules.
evidence: Part of the formal diagnosis of the taxon.

claim: Alasemenia has three broad wing-like integumentary lobes radially and symmetrically attached to each nucellus.
source: Three broad wing-like integumentary lobes radially and symmetrically attached to each nucellus, distally tapered and proximally reduced.
evidence: Part of the formal diagnosis of the taxon.

claim: The integumentary lobes of Alasemenia are distally tapered and proximally reduced.
source: Three broad wing-like integumentary lobes radially and symmetrically attached to each nucellus, distally tapered and proximally reduced.
evidence: Part of the formal diagnosis of the taxon.

claim: The integumentary lobes of Alasemenia evidently extend outwards, with their free parts ca. 40% of ovule length.
source: Integumentary lobes evidently extending outwards, with their free parts ca. 40% of ovule length.
evidence: Part of the formal diagnosis with quantitative measurement.

claim: Individual integumentary lobes of Alasemenia fold inwards along abaxial side.
source: Individual integumentary lobes folding inwards along abaxial side.
evidence: Part of the formal diagnosis of the taxon.

claim: The nucellus of Alasemenia is largely adnate to integument.
source: Nucellus largely adnate to integument.
evidence: Part of the formal diagnosis of the taxon.

claim: Some ovules of Alasemenia are borne terminally on smooth branches that are thrice dichotomous at 40–135°.
source: Some ovules are borne terminally on smooth branches that are thrice (Figure 1a), twice (Figure 1c) or once (Figure 1b, f, g and i, Figure 2a–c) dichotomous at 40–135°.
evidence: Direct observation with figure references and quantitative measurements.

claim: Some ovules of Alasemenia are borne terminally on smooth branches that are twice dichotomous at 40–135°.
source: Some ovules are borne terminally on smooth branches that are thrice (Figure 1a), twice (Figure 1c) or once (Figure 1b, f, g and i, Figure 2a–c) dichotomous at 40–135°.
evidence: Direct observation with figure references and quantitative measurements.

claim: Some ovules of Alasemenia are borne terminally on smooth branches that are once dichotomous at 40–135°.
source: Some ovules are borne terminally on smooth branches that are thrice (Figure 1a), twice (Figure 1c) or once (Figure 1b, f, g and i, Figure 2a–c) dichotomous at 40–135°.
evidence: Direct observation with figure references and quantitative measurements.

claim: The boundary between ovule and ultimate axis of Alasemenia refers to position where the ovule width just begins to increase.
source: The boundary between ovule and ultimate axis below refers to position where the ovule width just begins to increase (e.g. Figure 1a, arrow).
evidence: Direct definition with figure reference.

claim: The branches of Alasemenia excluding ovules are up to 76 mm long and 0.4–0.9 mm wide.
source: The branches excluding ovules are up to 76 mm long and 0.4–0.9 mm wide.
evidence: Direct quantitative measurement of fossil specimens.

claim: Most ovules of Alasemenia terminate ultimate axis.
source: Most ovules terminate ultimate axis (Figure 1j, Figure 2d–f) or are detached (Figure 1d, e, h and k, Figure 2g–o).
evidence: Direct observation with figure references.

claim: Some ovules of Alasemenia are detached.
source: Most ovules terminate ultimate axis (Figure 1j, Figure 2d–f) or are detached (Figure 1d, e, h and k, Figure 2g–o).
evidence: Direct observation with figure references.

claim: The ovules of Alasemenia are 25.0–33.0 mm long and 3.5–5.6 mm at the maximum width (excluding the width of outward extension of integumentary wings).
source: The ovules are 25.0–33.0 mm long and 3.5–5.6 mm at the maximum width (excluding the width of outward extension of integumentary wings).
evidence: Direct quantitative measurement of fossil specimens.

claim: Compressions of ovules of Alasemenia and their serial transverse sections do not show any cupules.
source: Compressions of ovules (Figure 1, Figure 2, Figure 3) and their serial transverse sections (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Figure 4—figure supplement 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 5) do not show any cupules.
evidence: Direct observation from fossil specimens and sections with figure references.

claim: Each ovule of Alasemenia possesses a layer of integument with three radially arranged and wing-like integumentary lobes.
source: Each ovule possesses a layer of integument with three radially arranged and wing-like integumentary lobes (Figure 1a, d and e, Figure 2d, e and o, arrows, Figure 3a–f, Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Figure 4—figure supplement 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Direct observation with extensive figure references.

claim: The integumentary lobes of Alasemenia are broad, acropetally tapered and proximally reduced to merge with the ultimate axis.
source: They are broad, acropetally tapered and proximally reduced to merge with the ultimate axis (Figure 1a–c and f, Figure 2a, d–i and n).
evidence: Direct observation with figure references.

claim: The integumentary lobes of Alasemenia are 1.2–2.3 mm at the maximum width and free for 8.3–14.8 mm distance (32–45% of the ovule length).
source: The integumentary lobes are 1.2–2.3 mm at the maximum width and free for 8.3–14.8 mm distance (32–45% of the ovule length), and the free lobe parts extend well above the nucellar tip and greatly curve outward.
evidence: Direct quantitative measurements from fossil specimens.

claim: The free lobe parts of Alasemenia extend well above the nucellar tip and greatly curve outward.
source: The integumentary lobes are 1.2–2.3 mm at the maximum width and free for 8.3–14.8 mm distance (32–45% of the ovule length), and the free lobe parts extend well above the nucellar tip and greatly curve outward.
evidence: Direct observation from fossil specimens.

claim: Usually, two lobes of a single Alasemenia ovule are evident and the third one is sometimes exposed through dégagement.
source: Usually, two lobes of a single ovule are evident and the third one is sometimes exposed through dégagement (Figure 1a, Figure 2n, arrow 2, o, middle arrow, Figure 3a and e, arrow).
evidence: Direct observation with figure references and description of preparation method.

claim: The lobes of an Alasemenia ovule are present on different bedding planes.
source: Such situation indicates that the lobes of an ovule are present on different bedding planes.
evidence: Inference from the observation that the third lobe is sometimes exposed through dégagement.

claim: In transverse sections of an Alasemenia ovule, two integumentary lobes extend along the bedding plane, and the third lobe is either originally perpendicular to or compressed to lie somewhat along the bedding plane.
source: In transverse sections of an ovule, two integumentary lobes extend along the bedding plane, and the third lobe is either originally perpendicular to or compressed to lie somewhat along the bedding plane (Figure 4c–e, h–k, n–r, t and w–y, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Figure 4—figure supplement 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Direct observation from transverse sections with figure references.

claim: The integumentary lobes of Alasemenia are narrow, flattened and fused in the lower part of an ovule, and acropetally become wide, thick, separated and far away.
source: The integumentary lobes are narrow, flattened and fused in the lower part of an ovule, and acropetally become wide, thick, separated and far away (Figure 4c–e, Figure 4—figure supplement 1a–k, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Direct observation from serial sections with figure references.

claim: Because of great outward curving of lobes, it is difficult to observe their distal parts in the sections of Alasemenia.
source: Because of great outward curving of lobes, it is difficult to observe their distal parts in the sections.
evidence: Direct statement about observational limitation.

claim: When thick, the lobes of Alasemenia present a V or U shape.
source: When thick, the lobes present a V or U shape.
evidence: Direct observation from sections.

claim: The lobes of Alasemenia are symmetrically folded along the abaxial side and toward the ovule center.
source: Therefore, they are symmetrically folded along the abaxial side and toward the ovule center.
evidence: Inference from the V or U shape observation.

claim: A few ovules of Alasemenia show the outline of a nucellus, which is ca. 10–11.7 mm long and 1.2–1.7 mm at the maximum width.
source: A few ovules show the outline of a nucellus, which is ca. 10–11.7 mm long and 1.2–1.7 mm at the maximum width (Figures 1d and 2i, arrows, j, Figure 3f–h).
evidence: Direct observation with quantitative measurements and figure references.

claim: Transverse sections of Alasemenia occasionally meet the nucellar tip.
source: Transverse sections occasionally meet the nucellar tip (Figure 4d, arrow).
evidence: Direct observation from sections with figure reference.

claim: With the exception of tip, the nucellus of Alasemenia is adnate to the integument and is distally surrounded by the free parts of integumentary lobes.
source: With the exception of tip, the nucellus is adnate to the integument and is distally surrounded by the free parts of integumentary lobes.
evidence: Direct observation from fossil specimens.

claim: Except few taxa including Guazia, Dorinnotheca, Cosmosperma, Elkinsia and Moresnetia, the earliest ovules in the Late Devonian (Famennian) have not been preserved to be connected to the branches.
source: Except few taxa including Guazia (Wang et al., 2022), Dorinnotheca (Fairon-Demaret, 1996), Cosmosperma (Liu et al., 2017), Elkinsia (Serbet and Rothwell, 1992) and Moresnetia (Fairon-Demaret and Scheckler, 1987), the earliest ovules in the Late Devonian (Famennian) have not been preserved to be connected to the branches.
evidence: Statement about the fossil record with multiple citations.

claim: Most Famennian ovules are usually surrounded by cupules.
source: These ovules are usually surrounded by cupules.
evidence: General statement about Famennian ovules based on the fossil record.

claim: The ovules of Alasemenia terminate the dichotomous branches and are transversely sectioned to show the ovular structures.
source: Now, as in Guazia, the ovules of Alasemenia terminate the dichotomous branches and are transversely sectioned to show the ovular structures.
evidence: Direct statement about the fossil preservation and preparation.

claim: The ovules of Alasemenia and Guazia provide rare evidence for acupulate ovules in the earliest seed plants.
source: The ovules of these two genera provide rare evidence for acupulate ovules in the earliest seed plants.
evidence: Inference from the fossil evidence of Alasemenia and Guazia.

claim: Both cupule and integument of an early ovule perform the protective and pollinating functions.
source: Both cupule and integument of an early ovule perform the protective and pollinating functions (Meyer-Berthaud, 2022).
evidence: Statement supported by citation.

claim: The integument of Alasemenia is adnate to most part of the nucellus and its three lobes extend long distance above the nucellar tip and then evidently outwards.
source: The integument of Alasemenia is adnate to most part of the nucellus and its three lobes extend long distance above the nucellar tip and then evidently outwards.
evidence: Direct observation from fossil specimens.

claim: The structure of Alasemenia integument leads to efficient protection of nucellus and adaptation for pollination.
source: Such structure leads to efficient protection of nucellus and adaptation for pollination.
evidence: Inference from the observed structure of the integument.

claim: In early seed plants, the fertile branches terminated by cupulate ovules consistently lack leaves.
source: In early seed plants, the fertile branches terminated by cupulate ovules consistently lack leaves and thus the cupules probably serve a nutritive function as in photosynthetic organs; this function may be transferred to the integuments of acupulate ovules such as Guazia (Meyer-Berthaud, 2022).
evidence: Statement about early seed plants with citation.

claim: The cupules of early seed plants probably serve a nutritive function as in photosynthetic organs.
source: In early seed plants, the fertile branches terminated by cupulate ovules consistently lack leaves and thus the cupules probably serve a nutritive function as in photosynthetic organs; this function may be transferred to the integuments of acupulate ovules such as Guazia (Meyer-Berthaud, 2022).
evidence: Inference with citation support.

claim: The nutritive function may be transferred to the integuments of acupulate ovules such as Guazia.
source: In early seed plants, the fertile branches terminated by cupulate ovules consistently lack leaves and thus the cupules probably serve a nutritive function as in photosynthetic organs; this function may be transferred to the integuments of acupulate ovules such as Guazia (Meyer-Berthaud, 2022).
evidence: Inference with citation support.

claim: The nutritive function would also apply to the integuments of Alasemenia since the acupulate ovules are terminal on various orders of naked branches and ultimate axes.
source: Regarding Alasemenia, the nutritive function would also apply to the integuments since the acupulate ovules are terminal on various orders of naked branches and ultimate axes.
evidence: Inference from the observed structure and comparison with other taxa.

claim: The surface of integuments of Alasemenia is enlarged through the outgrowths of wings and thus promotes the photosynthesis.
source: The surface of integuments is enlarged through the outgrowths of wings and thus promotes the photosynthesis.
evidence: Inference from the observed wing structure.

claim: Little is known about the dispersal function of Famennian ovules, because the integumentary wings as a derived character have been rarely documented.
source: Little is known about the dispersal function of Famennian ovules, because the integumentary wings as a derived character have been rarely documented.
evidence: Statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Warsteinia, Guazia and Alasemenia indicate that the anemochory originated in the Famennian.
source: Warsteinia (Rowe, 1997), Guazia (Wang et al., 2022) and now Alasemenia indicate that the anemochory originated in the Famennian.
evidence: Inference from the fossil evidence with citations.

claim: The ovule of Warsteinia remains unclear in attachment to branches and possession of a cupule.
source: However, the ovule of Warsteinia remains unclear in attachment to branches and possession of a cupule.
evidence: Statement about the limitations of Warsteinia fossil evidence.

claim: Alasemenia confirms that, like Guazia, the integuments of acupulate ovules developed a new function in wind dispersal.
source: Alasemenia confirms that, like Guazia, the integuments of acupulate ovules developed a new function in wind dispersal.
evidence: Inference from the fossil evidence of Alasemenia and comparison with Guazia.

claim: Besides Alasemenia, both Warsteinia and Guazia possess integumentary lobes forming radially arranged wings.
source: In the Late Devonian ovules, besides Alasemenia, both Warsteinia (Rowe, 1997) and Guazia (Wang et al., 2022) possess integumentary lobes forming radially arranged wings.
evidence: Statement about other Late Devonian ovules with citations.

claim: The integumentary wings of Late Devonian ovules illustrate diversity in number (three or four per ovule), length, folding or flattening, and being straight or curving distally.
source: Their integumentary wings illustrate diversity in number (three or four per ovule), length, folding or flattening, and being straight or curving distally.
evidence: Comparative statement about Late Devonian ovules.

claim: The integumentary wings of acupulate ovule of Guazia are broad, thin and fold inwards along the abaxial side.
source: As in Alasemenia (Figure 5a), the integumentary wings of acupulate ovule of Guazia are broad, thin and fold inwards along the abaxial side, but their numbers are four in each ovule and their free portions usually arch centripetally (Figure 5c; Wang et al., 2022, Figure 5).
evidence: Comparative statement with figure references and citation.

claim: Guazia has four integumentary wings in each ovule.
source: As in Alasemenia (Figure 5a), the integumentary wings of acupulate ovule of Guazia are broad, thin and fold inwards along the abaxial side, but their numbers are four in each ovule and their free portions usually arch centripetally (Figure 5c; Wang et al., 2022, Figure 5).
evidence: Comparative statement with figure references and citation.

claim: The free portions of Guazia integumentary wings usually arch centripetally.
source: As in Alasemenia (Figure 5a), the integumentary wings of acupulate ovule of Guazia are broad, thin and fold inwards along the abaxial side, but their numbers are four in each ovule and their free portions usually arch centripetally (Figure 5c; Wang et al., 2022, Figure 5).
evidence: Comparative statement with figure references and citation.

claim: Warsteinia has four integumentary wings without folding and their free portions are short and straight.
source: In contrast to Alasemenia, Warsteinia has four integumentary wings without folding and their free portions are short and straight (Rowe, 1997, TEXT-FIGURE 4).
evidence: Comparative statement with citation.

claim: Ovules of Alasemenia and Guazia terminating long and narrow branches suggest easy abscission of diaspores and better preparation for dispersal.
source: Ovules of Alasemenia and Guazia terminating long and narrow branches suggest easy abscission of diaspores (ovules with or without an ultimate axis) and better preparation for dispersal.
evidence: Inference from the observed morphology.

claim: Compared to Warsteinia with short and straight wings and Guazia with long but distally inwards curving wings, Alasemenia with longer and outwards extending wings would efficiently reduce the rate of descent and be more capably moved by wind.
source: Compared to Warsteinia with short and straight wings and Guazia with long but distally inwards curving wings, Alasemenia with longer and outwards extending wings would efficiently reduce the rate of descent and be more capably moved by wind.
evidence: Inference from comparative morphology.

claim: The quantitative analysis in mathematics indicates that three-winged ovules such as Alasemenia are more adapted to wind dispersal than four-winged ovules including Warsteinia and Guazia.
source: Furthermore, the quantitative analysis in mathematics indicates that three-winged ovules such as Alasemenia are more adapted to wind dispersal than four-winged ovules including Warsteinia and Guazia (see following).
evidence: Inference from mathematical analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Alasemenia, Guazia, and Warsteinia suggest that the evolutionarily novel wings, as integument outgrowths and the most important mechanism for seed dispersal by wind, appeared early in the spermatophytes and had been manifested in younger lineages.
source: Alasemenia, Guazia, and Warsteinia suggest that the evolutionarily novel wings, as integument outgrowths and the most important mechanism for seed dispersal by wind, appeared early in the spermatophytes and had been manifested in younger lineages.
evidence: Inference from the fossil evidence of these three taxa.

claim: Other wind dispersal mechanisms including plumes, pappi and parachutes of seeds appeared later in the Permo-Carboniferous and Mesozoic, respectively.
source: Other wind dispersal mechanisms including plumes, pappi and parachutes of seeds appeared later in the Permo-Carboniferous and Mesozoic, respectively (Axsmith et al., 2013).
evidence: Statement about the fossil record with citation.

claim: Current evidence indicates that seeds with three or four wings occurred first in the Late Devonian.
source: Current evidence indicates that seeds with three or four wings occurred first in the Late Devonian.
evidence: Summary statement based on the fossil evidence presented.

claim: Seeds with three or four wings were followed by two- or three-winged seeds in the Carboniferous.
source: They were followed by two- or three-winged seeds in the Carboniferous (Long, 1960; Long, 1969), and then by single-winged seeds in the Permian (Stevenson et al., 2015; Prevec et al., 2008).
evidence: Statement about the fossil record with citations.

claim: Two- or three-winged seeds were followed by single-winged seeds in the Permian.
source: They were followed by two- or three-winged seeds in the Carboniferous (Long, 1960; Long, 1969), and then by single-winged seeds in the Permian (Stevenson et al., 2015; Prevec et al., 2008).
evidence: Statement about the fossil record with citations.

claim: Relating to wind dispersal, the diaspores (seeds/fruits) of living spermatophytes possess multiple mechanisms and variable number of wings.
source: Relating to wind dispersal, the diaspores (seeds/fruits) of living spermatophytes possess multiple mechanisms and variable number of wings (Ma, 2009).
evidence: Statement about living plants with citation.

claim: The rate of diaspore descent in still air is an important indicator of the potential ability of modern samaras dispersal.
source: The rate of diaspore descent in still air is an important indicator of the potential ability of modern samaras dispersal (Augspurger et al., 2016; Augspurger et al., 2017).
evidence: Statement about modern samaras with citations.

claim: Terminal velocity is used as an indicator of dispersal ability for ovules.
source: As for ovules, we also use terminal velocity as an indicator of dispersal ability.
evidence: Statement about the analytical approach used in the study.

claim: The wing loading of Alasemenia is obviously less than that of Guazia.
source: Since the broad integumentary wings well extend outwards, the wing loading of Alasemenia is obviously less than that of Guazia.
evidence: Inference from the observed morphology.

claim: When the winged seeds fall in the air, the predictable spinning can lead to the reduction of fall rate, and result in the increase of the horizontal dispersal distance.
source: When the winged seeds fall in the air, the predictable spinning can lead to the reduction of fall rate, and result in the increase of the horizontal dispersal distance. This has been observed in the field experiments or proved in the modelling reconstruction experiments (Green, 1980; Habgood et al., 1998).
evidence: Statement about seed dispersal with citations.

claim: The tiny asymmetry of ovules will be amplified in the running geometry by centrifugal and aerodynamic loads, result in vibrations and thus significantly reduce the efficiency.
source: However, the tiny asymmetry of ovules will be amplified in the running geometry by centrifugal and aerodynamic loads, result in vibrations and thus significantly reduce the efficiency (Lu et al., 2019).
evidence: Statement about aerodynamics with citation.

claim: In the ovules with even number of wings like Guazia and Warsteinia, the center symmetry structure will lead to stronger resonance than the ovules with odd number of wings (like Alasemenia).
source: In the ovules with even number of wings like Guazia (Wang et al., 2022) and Warsteinia (Rowe, 1992; Rowe, 1997), the center symmetry structure will lead to stronger resonance than the ovules with odd number of wings (like Alasemenia).
evidence: Inference from aerodynamic principles with citations.

claim: The ovules with odd number of wings are more stable in high rate spinning and spend more falling time in the dispersal process.
source: It means the ovules with odd number of wings are more stable in high rate spinning and spend more falling time in the dispersal process.
evidence: Inference from the resonance analysis.

claim: For ovules, the Reynolds numbers are mainly falling in 103–104, suggesting that the inertia forces are much stronger than viscous forces.
source: The Reynolds number (Re) is the indicator of patterns in fluid flow situations, and for ovules, the Reynolds numbers are mainly falling in 103–104, suggesting that the inertia forces are much stronger than viscous forces (Burrows, 1975; Seter and Rosen, 1992).
evidence: Statement about fluid dynamics with citations.

claim: The relative efficiency for wind dispersal (Er) of one- to four-winged seeds in five ideal basic situations is calculated for comparison.
source: Generally, the above one- to four-winged seeds are quantitatively analysed for their wind dispersal capability and the results are shown in Figure 6. The relative efficiency for wind dispersal (Er) of these seeds in five ideal basic situations is calculated for comparison.
evidence: Statement about the mathematical analysis with figure reference.

claim: The one- or two-winged seeds are treated as a control group when the wings keep facing the wind and do not rotate, and in this case, the value of Er is 100%.
source: The one- or two-winged seeds are treated as a control group when the wings keep facing the wind and do not rotate. In this case, the value of Er is 100%.
evidence: Statement about the mathematical analysis setup.

claim: When descending through autorotation, one- to four-winged seeds present different values of Er.
source: When descending through autorotation, one- to four-winged seeds present different values of Er.
evidence: Statement about the mathematical analysis results.

claim: The relative wind dispersal efficiency of three-winged seeds is obviously better than that of single- and two-winged seeds, and is close to that of four-winged seeds.
source: The relative wind dispersal efficiency of three-winged seeds is obviously better than that of single- and two-winged seeds, and is close to that of four-winged seeds (Figure 6).
